 263+ 0000
 264+ 0000
 265+ 0000              ; Reading a next register is two port accesses: select it on $243B, then read $253B. The IM2 handler reads MMU7 the same
 266+ 0000              ; way (SaveMMU7), so an interrupt between the two would leave MMU7 selected and the read would return its value instead
 267+ 0000              ; (seen on hardware as phantom extended key presses: BankKeyboard in MMU7 reads as EDIT, the system map). So in main
 268+ 0000              ; line code the pair runs with interrupts off. These re-enable them (ei) so must not be used where interrupts are off,
 269+ 0000              ; i.e. in the IM2 handler or anything it calls, or startup before interrupts are on: use GetNextRegNoInt there.
 270+ 0000              GetNextRegSaveBC:	MACRO register
 271+ 0000 ~                                push bc
 272+ 0000 ~                                ld bc,$243B
 273+ 0000 ~                                ld a,register
 274+ 0000 ~                                di
 275+ 0000 ~                                out (c),a
 276+ 0000 ~                                inc b
 277+ 0000 ~                                in a,(c)
 278+ 0000 ~                                ei
 279+ 0000 ~                                pop bc
 280+ 0000                                  ENDM
 281+ 0000
 282+ 0000              GetNextReg:	MACRO register
 283+ 0000 ~                        ld bc,$243B
 284+ 0000 ~                        ld a,register
 285+ 0000 ~                        di
 286+ 0000 ~                        out (c),a
 287+ 0000 ~                        inc b
 288+ 0000 ~                        in a,(c)
 289+ 0000 ~                        ei
 290+ 0000                          ENDM
 291+ 0000
 292+ 0000              ; for code that runs with interrupts already off (the IM2 handler and what it calls), so nothing can interrupt the pair
 293+ 0000              GetNextRegNoInt: MACRO register
 294+ 0000 ~                        ld bc,$243B
 295+ 0000 ~                        ld a,register
 296+ 0000 ~                        out (c),a
 297+ 0000 ~                        inc b
 298+ 0000 ~                        in a,(c)
 299+ 0000                          ENDM
 300+ 0000
# file closed: Hardware/register_defines.asm

  35+ 0000              ;-- Name: LL28 Calculate R = 256 * A / Q
  36+ 0000              ;-- LL28+4              Skips the A >= Q check and always returns with C flag cleared, so this can be called if we know the division will work
  37+ 0000              ;-- LL31                Skips the A >= Q check and does not set the R counter, so this can be used for jumping straight into the division loop if R is already set to 254 and we know the division will work
  38+ 0000              ;   Reg mapping 6502  Z80
  39+ 0000              ;               a     a
  40+ 0000              ;               b     x
  41+ 0000              ;               c     q
  42+ 0000              ;               d     r
  43+ 0000              ;
  44+ 0000              ClippingCodeLL28Macro:      MACRO   prefix1?
  45+ 0000 ~            prefix1?_LL28_6502:         ld      hl,Qvar                 ; CMP Q                  \ If A >= Q, then the answer will not fit in one byte,
  46+ 0000 ~                                        ld      c,(hl)                  ; using c as Q var
  47+ 0000 ~                                        cp      c
  48+ 0000 ~                                        FlipCarryFlag
  49+ 0000 ~                                        jp      c, prefix1?_LL2_6502    ; BCS LL2                \ so jump to LL2 to return 255
  50+ 0000 ~                                        ld      b,$FE                   ; LDX #%11111110         \ Set R to have bits 1-7 set, so we can rotate through 7 loop iterations, getting a 1 each time, and then we use b as Rvar
  51+ 0000 ~            prefix1?_LL31_6502:          sla     a                       ; ASL A                  \ Shift A to the left
  52+ 0000 ~                                        jp      c, prefix1?_LL29_6502             ; BCS LL29               \ If bit 7 of A was set, then jump straight to the subtraction
  53+ 0000 ~                                        FlipCarryFlag                   ;                          If A < N, then C flag is set.
  54+ 0000 ~                                        JumpIfALTNusng c, prefix1?_LL31_SKIPSUB_6502 ; CMP Q              \ If A < Q, skip the following subtraction
  55+ 0000 ~                                                                            ; BCC P%+4
  56+ 0000 ~                                        sub     c                       ; SBC Q                  \ A >= Q, so set A = A - Q
  57+ 0000 ~                                        ClearCarryFlag
  58+ 0000 ~            prefix1?_LL31_SKIPSUB_6502:  FlipCarryFlag
  59+ 0000 ~                                        rl      b                       ; ROL R                  \ Rotate the counter in R to the left, and catch the result bit into bit 0 (which will be a 0 if we didn't do the subtraction, or 1 if we did)
  60+ 0000 ~                                        jp      c, prefix1?_LL31_6502            ; BCS LL31               \ If we still have set bits in R, loop back to LL31 to do the next iteration of 7
  61+ 0000 ~                                        ld      a,b
  62+ 0000 ~                                        ld      (Rvar),a
  63+ 0000 ~                                        ret                             ; RTS                    \ R left with remainder of division
  64+ 0000 ~            prefix1?_LL29_6502:          sub     c                       ; SBC Q                  \ A >= Q, so set A = A - Q
  65+ 0000 ~                                        SetCarryFlag                    ; SEC                    \ Set the C flag to rotate into the result in R
  66+ 0000 ~                                        rl      b                       ; ROL R                  \ Rotate the counter in R to the left, and catch the result bit into bit 0 (which will be a 0 if we didn't do the subtraction, or 1 if we did)
  67+ 0000 ~                                        jp      c, prefix1?_LL31_6502            ; BCS LL31               \ If we still have set bits in R, loop back to LL31 to do the next iteration of 7
  68+ 0000 ~                                        ld      a,b                     ; RTS                    \ Return from the subroutine with R containing the

  72+ 0000 ~                                        ld      (Rvar),a                ; STA R                  \ possible answer to 256, i.e. R = 255
  73+ 0000 ~                                        SetCarryFlag                    ; we failed so need carry flag set
  74+ 0000 ~                                        ret                             ; RTS                    \ Return from the subroutine

 144+ 0000                              ;--- LL118 Move along a point until on screen
 145+ 0000              ; In XX1510 x1 as a 16-bit coordinate (x1_hi x1_lo)
 146+ 0000              ;    XX1532 y1 as a 16-bit coordinate (y1_hi y1_lo)
 147+ 0000              ;    XX12p2 The line's gradient * 256 (so 1.0 = 256)
 148+ 0000              ;    XX12p3 The direction of slope: * Positive = top left to bottom right * Negative (bit 7 set) = top right to bottom left
 149+ 0000              ;    T      The gradient of slope:* 0 if it's a shallow slope * &FF if it's a steep slope
 150+ 0000              ;  Out  XX150               x1 as an 8-bit coordinate
 151+ 0000              ;       XX152               y1 as an 8-bit coordinate
 152+ 0000              ;----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
 153+ 0000
 154+ 0000
 155+ 0000              ;---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
 156+ 0000              ;--  Calculate the following:
 157+ 0000              ;--   * If T = 0, this is a shallow slope, so calculate (Y X) = (S x1_lo) * XX12+2
 158+ 0000              ;--   * If T <> 0, this is a steep slope, so calculate (Y X) = (S x1_lo) / XX12+2
 159+ 0000              ;-- giving (Y X) the opposite sign to the slope direction in XX12+3.
 160+ 0000              ;---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
 161+ 0000              ClippingCodeLL120Macro:     MACRO   prefix1?
 162+ 0000 ~            prefix1?_LL120_6502:        ld      a,(prefix1?_XX1510)              ;LDA XX15               \ Set R = x1_lo
 163+ 0000 ~                                        ld      (Rvar),a                ;STA R
 164+ 0000 ~                                        call    prefix1?_LL129_6502              ;JSR LL129              \ Call LL129 to do the following:  Q = XX12+2 = line gradient, A = S EOR XX12+3 = S EOR slope direction  (S R) = |S R|
 165+ 0000 ~                                        push    af                      ;PHA                    \ Store A on the stack so we can use it later
 166+ 0000 ~            ; DONT NEED PLUS MESSES UP FLAGS                    push    af                      ;LDX T                  \ If T is non-zero, then it's a steep slope, so jump
 167+ 0000 ~                                        ld      a,(Tvar)                ; .
 168+ 0000 ~                                        ld      (Xreg),a                ;. REDUNDANT REMOVE IN OPTIMISATION
 169+ 0000 ~                                        and     a                       ;BNE LL121              \ down to LL121 to calculate this instead (Y X) = (S R) / Q
 170+ 0000 ~            ; DONT NEED PLUS MESSES UP FLAGS                    pop     af                      ;.                      (recover teh saved A before the cp)
 171+ 0000 ~                                        jr      nz,prefix1?_LL121_6502           ;.
 172+ 0000 ~            ;..   (Y X) = (S R) * Q - must be ABS, sign determined by opposite of the sign of the value on top of stack
 173+ 0000 ~            prefix1?_LL122_6502:         ZeroA                           ;LDA #0                 \ Set A = 0
 174+ 0000 ~
 175+ 0000 ~                                        IFDEF DEBUG_LL122_DIRECT"
 176+ 0000 ~                                              DISPLAY "DIRECT CALL TO LL122 so dummy push a to stack with 0"
 177+ 0000 ~                                              push    af
 178+ 0000 ~                                        ENDIF
 179+ 0000 ~                                        ld      (Xreg),a                ;TAX                    \ Set (Y X) = 0 so we can start building the answer here
 180+ 0000 ~                                        ld      (Yreg),a                ;TAY
 181+ 0000 ~                                        ld      hl,Svar
 182+ 0000 ~                                        ld      bc,(SRvarPair)          ;LSR S                  \ Shift (S R) to the right, so we extract bit 0 of (S R)
 183+ 0000 ~                                        ShiftBCRight1                   ;ROR R                  \ into the C flag
 184+ 0000 ~                                        ld      (SRvarPair),bc
 185+ 0000 ~                                        ld      hl, Qvar                ;ASL Q                  \ Shift Q to the left, catching bit 7 in the C flag
 186+ 0000 ~                                        sla     (hl)                    ;.
 187+ 0000 ~                                        jr      nc, prefix1?_LL126_6502          ;BCC LL126              \ If C (i.e. the next bit from Q) is clear, do not do
 188+ 0000 ~            ; the addition for this bit of Q, and instead skip to LL126 to just do the shifts
 189+ 0000 ~            prefix1?_LL125_6502:        call    AddSRToYX               ;TXA                    \ Set (Y X) = (Y X) + (S R)  starting with the low bytes And then doing the high bytes
 190+ 0000 ~            prefix1?_LL126_6502:        ld      bc,(SRvarPair)          ;LSR S                  \ Shift (S R) to the right
 191+ 0000 ~                                        ShiftBCRight1                   ;ROR R
 192+ 0000 ~                                        ld      (SRvarPair),bc          ;.
 193+ 0000 ~                                        ld      hl, Qvar                ;ASL Q                  \ Shift Q to the left, catching bit 7 in the C flag
 194+ 0000 ~                                        sla     (hl)                    ;.
 195+ 0000 ~                                        jr      c,prefix1?_LL125_6502            ;BCS LL125              \ If C (i.e. the next bit from Q) is set, loop back to LL125 to do the addition for this bit of Q
 196+ 0000 ~                                        jr      nz,prefix1?_LL126_6502           ;BNE LL126              \ If Q has not yet run out of set bits, loop back to LL126 to do the \"shift\" part of shift-and-add until we have done additions for all the set bits in Q, to give us our multiplication result
 197+ 0000 ~                                        pop     af                      ;PLA                    \ Restore A, which we calculated above, from the stack
 198+ 0000 ~                                        and     a                       ;BPL LL133              \ If A is positive jump to LL133 to negate (Y X) and
 199+ 0000 ~                                        jp      p,prefix1?_LL133_6502            ;.

 204+ 0000              ;-- Calculate the following:
 205+ 0000              ;--         * If T = 0, this is a shallow slope, so calculate (Y X) = (S R) / XX12+2 (does not use X1lo but directly SR)
 206+ 0000              ;--         * If T <> 0, this is a steep slope, so calculate (Y X) = (S R) * XX12+2  (does not use X1lo but directly SR)

 208+ 0000              ClippingCodeLL122Macro:      MACRO   prefix1?

 212+ 0000 ~                                         ld      a,(Tvar)                ; .

 214+ 0000 ~                                         and     a                       ;.
 215+ 0000 ~            ;  DONT NEED PLUS MESSES UP FLAGS                    pop     af                      ;.
 216+ 0000 ~                                         jr      nz,prefix1?_LL122_6502           ;.
 217+ 0000 ~            ;--  The following calculates: (Y X) = (S R) / Q using the same shift-and-subtract algorithm that's documented in TIS2
 218+ 0000 ~            prefix1?_LL121_6502:         ld      a,$FF                   ;LDA #%11111111         \ Set Y = %11111111
 219+ 0000 ~                                         ld      (Yreg),a                ;TAY
 220+ 0000 ~                                         sla     a                       ;ASL A                  \ Set X = %11111110
 221+ 0000 ~                                         ld      (Xreg),a                ;TAX
 222+ 0000 ~            ;--  This sets (Y X) = %1111111111111110, so we can rotate through 15 loop iterations, getting a 1 each time, and then getting a 0 on the 16th iteration... and we can also use it to catch our result bits into bit 0 each time
 223+ 0000 ~            prefix1?_LL130_6502:         ld      bc,(SRvarPair)          ;ASL R                  \ Shift (S R) to the left
 224+ 0000 ~                                        ShiftBCLeft1                    ;.
 225+ 0000 ~                                        ld      (SRvarPair),bc          ;ROL S
 226+ 0000 ~                                        ld      a,(Svar)                ;LDA S                  \ Set A = S
 227+ 0000 ~                                        jr      c, prefix1?_LL131_6502           ;BCS LL131              \ If bit 7 of S was set, then jump straight to the subtraction
 228+ 0000 ~                                        ld      hl,Qvar                 ;CMP Q                  \ If A < Q (i.e. S < Q), skip the following subtractions
 229+ 0000 ~                                        cp      (hl)
 230+ 0000 ~                                        FlipCarryFlag                   ; note flip carry flag here to simulate 6502 operation
 231+ 0000 ~                                        jr      nc,prefix1?_LL132A_6502          ;BCC LL132  (NOTE Carry flag reversed in Z80 for CP)
 232+ 0000 ~            prefix1?_LL131_6502:         FlipCarryFlag                   ;flip carry to make it act like a 6502 borrow
 233+ 0000 ~                                        sbc     (hl)                    ;SBC Q                  \ A >= Q (i.e. S >= Q) so set:
 234+ 0000 ~                                        ld      (Svar),a                ;STA S
 235+ 0000 ~                                        ld      a,(Rvar)                ;LDA R                  \ And then doing the high bytes
 236+ 0000 ~                                        ClearCarryFlag                  ;\   S = (A R) - Q  = (S R) - Q starting with the low bytes (we know the C flag is set so the subtraction will be correct)
 237+ 0000 ~                                        sbc     0                       ;SBC #0

 243+ 0000 ~                                        RollBCLeft1                     ; ROL A                  \ result bit into bit 0 (which will be a 0 if we didn't
 244+ 0000 ~                                        ld      (YXregPair),bc          ; TAX                    \ do the subtraction, or 1 if we did)
 245+ 0000 ~                                        jr      c, prefix1?_LL130_6502           ; BCS LL130              \ If we still have set bits in (Y X), loop back to LL130 to do the next iteration of 15, until we have done the whole division
 246+ 0000 ~                    IFDEF DEBUG_LL121_DIRECT
 247+ 0000 ~                          DISPLAY "DIRECT CALL TO LL121 so dummy push"
 248+ 0000 ~                                        push    af
 249+ 0000 ~                    ENDIF

 251+ 0000 ~                                        and     a                       ; BMI LL128              \ If A is negative jump to LL128 to return from the
 252+ 0000 ~                                        jp      m, prefix1?_LL128_6502           ; .                      \ subroutine with (Y X) as is
 253+ 0000 ~            prefix1?_LL133_6502:          ld      bc,(YXregPair)          ; TXA                    \ Otherwise negate (Y X) using two's complement by first
 254+ 0000 ~                                        macronegate16bc                 ; EOR #%11111111         \ setting the low byte to ~X + 1
 255+ 0000 ~                                        ld      (YXregPair),bc          ; ADC #1                 \ The addition works as we know the C flag is clear from\ when we passed through the BCS above
 256+ 0000 ~            prefix1?_LL128_6502:          ret                             ; RTS                    \ Return from the subroutine
 257+ 0000 ~            ;-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
 258+ 0000 ~            ;..  Do the following, in this order: Q = XX12+2 A = S EOR XX12+3 (S R) = |S R|

 506+ 0000 ~                                        jp      prefix1?_LL116_6502     ; JMP LL116              \ Jump to LL116, as we now have the line's gradient in R
 507+ 0000 ~            ;-- If we get here then our line is more vertical than horizontal, so it is a steep slope
 508+ 0000 ~            prefix1?_LL114_6502:        ld      a,(delta_y)             ; LDA XX12+4             \ Set Q = delta_y_lo
 509+ 0000 ~                                        ld      (Qvar),a                ; STA Q
 510+ 0000 ~                                        ld      a,(delta_x)             ; LDA XX12+2             \ Set A = delta_x_lo
 511+ 0000 ~                                        call    prefix1?_LL28_6502               ; JSR LL28               \ Call LL28 to calculate: R = 256 * A / Q = 256 * delta_x_lo / delta_y_lo
 512+ 0000 ~                                        ld      a,$FF                   ; DEC T                  \ T was set to 0 above, so this sets T = &FF when our
 513+ 0000 ~                                        ld      (Tvar),a                ;                        \ line is steep
 514+ 0000 ~            ;----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
 515+ 0000 ~            ;--- LL116 This part sets things up to call the routine in LL188, which does the actual clipping.
 516+ 0000 ~            ;--  If we get here, then R has been set to the gradient of the line (x1, y1) to(x2, y2), with T indicating the gradient of slope: * 0   = shallow slope (more horizontal than vertical)
 517+ 0000 ~            ;--                                                                                                                                * &FF = steep slope (more vertical than horizontal)
 518+ 0000 ~            ;-- XX13 has been set as follows: * 0   = (x1, y1) off-screen, (x2, y2) on-screen * 95(64)  = (x1, y1) on-screen,  (x2, y2) off-screen * 191(128) = (x1, y1) off-screen, (x2, y2) off-screen
 519+ 0000 ~            prefix1?_LL116_6502:        ld      a,(Rvar)                ; LDA R                  \ Store the gradient in XX12+2
 520+ 0000 ~                                        ld      (prefix1?_XX12p2),a     ; STA XX12+2
 521+ 0000 ~                                        ld      a,(Svar)                ; LDA S                  \ Store the type of slope in XX12+3, bit 7 clear means
 522+ 0000 ~                                        ld      (prefix1?_XX12p3),a              ; STA XX12+3             \ top left to bottom right, bit 7 set means top right to bottom left
 523+ 0000 ~                                        ld      a,( prefix1?_XX13)                ; LDA XX13               \ If XX13 = 0, skip the following instruction
 524+ 0000 ~                                        cp      0                       ; BEQ LL138
 525+ 0000 ~                                        jp      z,prefix1?_LL138_6502            ; .
 526+ 0000 ~                                        jp      p, prefix1?_LLX117_6502          ; If XX13 is positive, it must be 95 (64) as 128 would be negative). This means (x1, y1) is on-screen but (x2, y2) isn't, so we jump
 527+ 0000 ~            ;-- If we get here, XX13 = 0 or 191, so (x1, y1) is off-screen and needs clipping
 528+ 0000 ~            prefix1?_LL138_6502:          call    prefix1?_LL118_6502              ; JSR LL118              \ Call LL118 to move (x1, y1) along the line onto the screen, i.e. clip the line at the (x1, y1) end
 529+ 0000 ~                                        ld      a,( prefix1?_XX13)                ; LDA XX13               \ If XX13 = 0, i.e. (x2, y2) is on-screen, jump down to
 530+ 0000 ~                                        and     a
 531+ 0000 ~                                        jp      p,prefix1?_LL124_6502            ; BPL LL124              \ LL124 to return with a successfully clipped line
 532+ 0000 ~            ;-- If we get here, XX13 = 191 (128) (both coordinates areoff-screen)
 533+ 0000 ~            prefix1?_LL117_6502:          ld      a,(prefix1?_XX1510+1)            ; LDA XX15+1             \ If either of x1_hi or y1_hi are non-zero, jump to
 534+ 0000 ~                                        ld      hl,prefix1?_XX1532+1             ; ORA XX15+3             \ LL137 to return from the subroutine with the C flag
 535+ 0000 ~                                        or      (hl)
 536+ 0000 ~                                        jp      nz, prefix1?_LL137_6502          ; BNE LL137              \ set, as the line doesn't fit on-screen
 537+ 0000 ~                                        ld      a,(prefix1?_XX1532)              ; LDA XX15+2             \ If y1_lo > y-coordinate of the bottom of the screen
 538+ 0000 ~                                        cp      128                     ; CMP #Y*2               \ jump to LL137 to return from the subroutine with the
 539+ 0000 ~                                        jp      nc, prefix1?_LL137_6502          ; BCS LL137              \ C flag set, as the line doesn't fit on-screen
 540+ 0000 ~            ;-- If we get here, XX13 = 95 or 191, and in both cases (x2, y2) is off-screen, so we now need to swap the (x1, y1) and (x2, y2) coordinates around before doing the actual clipping, because we need to clip (x2, y2) but the clipping routine at LL118 only clips (x1, y1)
 541+ 0000 ~            prefix1?_LLX117_6502:         ld      hl,( prefix1?_XX1510)             ; LDX XX15               \ Swap x1_lo = x2_lo
 542+ 0000 ~                                        ld      de,( prefix1?_XX1554)
 543+ 0000 ~                                        ld      ( prefix1?_XX1510),de
 544+ 0000 ~                                        ld      ( prefix1?_XX1554),hl
 545+ 0000 ~                                        ld      hl,( prefix1?_XX1532)             ; LDX XX15+2             \ Swap y1_lo = y2_lo
 546+ 0000 ~                                        ld      de,( prefix1?_XX1576)
 547+ 0000 ~                                        ld      ( prefix1?_XX1532),de
 548+ 0000 ~                                        ld      ( prefix1?_XX1576),hl
 549+ 0000 ~                                        call    prefix1?_LL118_6502              ; JSR LL118              \ Call LL118 to move (x1, y1) along the line onto the screen, i.e. clip the line at the (x1, y1) end
 550+ 0000 ~                                        ld      hl,SWAP
 551+ 0000 ~                                        dec     (hl)                    ; DEC SWAP               \ Set SWAP = &FF to indicate that we just clipped the line at the (x2, y2) end by swapping the coordinates (the DEC does this as we set SWAP to 0 at the start of this subroutine)
 552+ 0000 ~            prefix1?_LL124_6502:          pop     af                      ; PLA            SP+0    \ Restore Y from the stack so it gets preserved through
 553+ 0000 ~                                        ld      (Yreg),a                ; TAY                    \ the call to this subroutine
 554+ 0000 ~                                        call    prefix1?_LL146_6502              ; JMP LL146              \ Jump up to LL146 to move the low bytes of (x1, y1) and (x2, y2) into (X1, Y1) and (X2, Y2), and return from the subroutine with a successfully clipped line
 555+ 0000 ~                                        ret                             ; then exit so we don't pop it twice
 556+ 0000 ~            prefix1?_LL137_6502:          pop     af                      ; PLA            SP+0    \ Restore Y from the stack so it gets preserved through
 557+ 0000 ~                                        ld      (Yreg),a                ; TAY                    \ the call to this subroutine
 558+ 0000 ~                                        SetCarryFlag                    ; SEC                    \ Set the C flag to indicate the clipped line does not fit on-screen
 559+ 0000 ~                                        ret                             ; RTS                    \ Return from the subroutine

 565+ 0000 ~                                        ldir

 567+ 0000 ~                                        ret     c                               ; returns if carry is set as its a no draw

  89+ 0000              ; Sets IYH to sign bits, bit 7 = x, bit 6 = y bit 5 = z
  90+ 0000              SetIYHToSignBits:       MACRO
  91+ 0000 ~                                    ld      a,(ix+POS_ZSGNOFFSET)   ; get Z sign
  92+ 0000 ~                                    and     $80                     ; and shift it via A into IYH bit 7
  93+ 0000 ~                                    srl     a                       ;
  94+ 0000 ~                                    ld      iyh,a                   ;
  95+ 0000 ~                                    ld      a,(ix+POS_YSGNOFFSET)   ; get Y sign
  96+ 0000 ~                                    and     $80                     ; and shift it via A into IYH bit 7
  97+ 0000 ~                                    or      iyh                     ; which moves Z into IYH bit 6
  98+ 0000 ~                                    srl     a                       ;
  99+ 0000 ~                                    ld      iyh,a                   ;
 100+ 0000 ~                                    ld      a,(ix+POS_XSGNOFFSET)   ; get X sign
 101+ 0000 ~                                    and     $80                     ; and shift it via A into IYH bit 7
 102+ 0000 ~                                    or      iyh                     ; which moves Y into IYH bit 6 and Z into IYH bit 5
 103+ 0000 ~                                    ld      iyh,a                   ;
 104+ 0000                                      ENDM

 275+ 6097              ;----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
 276+ 6097              ; Laser, once a main loop. Times are 50 Hz frames of FrameCounter16 (the interrupt's count, stopped while paused), so a
 277+ 6097              ; pulse lasts as long however fast the loop runs. Like Z-Police's game clock (clock_step): dt = the frames since the last
 278+ 6097              ; update (at most LaserMaxFrames, so a stall doesn't jump), and each state's end is a frame number, compared by 16 bit
 279+ 6097              ; subtraction so it works across the counter's wrap.
 280+ 6097              ;   LaserReady  fire held (LaserFireHeld, from the front view's keys) starts a burst of CurrLaserPulseRate pulses,
 281+ 6097              ;               or with a rate of 0 a beam
 282+ 6097              ;   LaserOn     a pulse, CurrLaserPulseOnTime frames; a beam stays on while fire is held
 283+ 6097              ;   LaserOff    CurrLaserPulseOffTime frames between a burst's pulses
 284+ 6097              ;   LaserRest   CurrLaserPulseRest frames after a burst (or a beam) before the next
 285+ 6097              ; Out: LaserBeamOn (the sprite), LaserHitDamage (what a ship in the sights takes this loop: a pulse's damage when it
 286+ 6097              ; starts, a beam's for each frame it was on), energy drained and heat added for each frame on, the gun cooled for each
 287+ 6097              ; frame off. LaserFireHeld is cleared: the keys set it again each loop while fire is held.
 288+ 6097              LaserReady              equ 0
 289+ 6097              LaserOn                 equ 1
 290+ 6097              LaserOff                equ 2
 291+ 6097              LaserRest               equ 3
 292+ 6097              LaserMaxFrames          equ 8

 485+ 622D              ; The space station's safe zone (as BBC Elite): inside the cube |x|, |y|, |z| < $C000 round the planet (sign bytes no
 486+ 622D              ; integer bits, hi bytes < $C0). SpaceStationSafeZone is 0 inside, $FF outside (SetSafeZone / ClearSafeZone); the spawn
 487+ 622D              ; tables, the status screen and the station's arrival use it. On flying in, if slot 0 (kept for it) is free, the station
 488+ 622D              ; is made there: on the line from the planet's centre towards us, |normal| * 192 out (49000 at most, as BBC's 2 nosev

  87+ 6501              ; The integer part of each S15.8 axis is the sign byte bits 0-6 (upper) and the hi byte (lower); an axis is far enough
  88+ 6501              ; away if the upper byte is non zero or the lower byte is > 1, and one far axis is enough to allow the warp.

   2+ 6A29              ; The hyperspace countdown, timed by FrameCounter16 (the interrupt's 50 Hz count, which stops while paused) so a second is
   3+ 6A29              ; a second however fast the main loop runs. OuterHyperCount is the seconds left, shown 11 to 1; the jump starts when it
   4+ 6A29              ; would reach 0. InnerHyperCount is non zero while counting (ViewKeyTest and the warp key test the pair as a word).
   5+ 6A29              ; HyperSpaceMessage (main loop, views) draws the text every loop and clears it once when the count stops.
   6+ 6A29

 189+ 7054              ;----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
 190+ 7054              ; DrawSunDistance / DrawPlanetDistance / DrawStationDistance: print the integer part of the distance to the sun, planet
 191+ 7054              ; and space station on layer 2 to the right of their compass sprites.
 192+ 7054              ; The compass sprites sit in the left border (sprite x 0-33, top y = Sun/Planet/StationCompassTLY, layer 2 is offset by
 193+ 7054              ; 32,32 from sprite coordinates), so the text goes at the left of the 3D view, centred on each compass where possible.
 194+ 7054              ; That area is cleared every frame, so these are called every frame from the main loop rather than from UpdateConsole,
 195+ 7054              ; which only runs on console refresh frames.
 196+ 7054              ; Distance ~= max + 3/8 (mid + min) of |x|, |y|, |z| (within about +13% / -3%), using the integer part of each
 197+ 7054              ; S15.8 position (sign byte bits 0-6 and the hi byte), so it fits 16 bits (max 57341)
 198+ 7054              DistanceCol             equ 4
 199+ 7054              SunDistanceRow          equ 2                                       ; sun compass centre is above layer 2, so top text row
 200+ 7054              PlanetDistanceRow       equ PlanetCompassTLY + 17 - 32 - 4          ; compass centre (top + 17) in layer 2 rows, less half a character
 201+ 7054              StationDistanceRow      equ StationCompassTLY + 17 - 32 - 4
 202+ 7054              SunDistanceColour       equ L2ColourYELLOW_1
 203+ 7054              PlanetDistanceColour    equ L2ColourGREEN_1
 204+ 7054              StationDistanceColour   equ L2ColourWHITE_1

 860+ 74F7              ; Compass dot offsets: B = Y, C = X, 2's complement, +/-12 at 90 degrees off (the sun from NormalToCompassSigned, the

1255+ 78C8              ; Radar edge markers: when the sun, planet or space station is outside the scanner range in X or Z (|x| or |z| >= 64,
1256+ 78C8              ; the same limit the blips use, y is ignored) a dot is put on the scanner outline in its direction. The direction is the
1257+ 78C8              ; one a blip would use (column = x, row = z / 4) and the ray is stepped out a row at a time until it reaches the outline.
1258+ 78C8              ; The outline is not a true ellipse so its half widths are tabled, measured from the console image: columns 59-196,
1259+ 78C8              ; rows 155-190, centre 127.5, 172.5 (left and right are symmetric about it)
1260+ 78C8              RadarEdgeRowAbove       equ 172                         ; k rows up from here for objects in front (z +ve)

1263+ 78C8              RadarEdgeColLeft        equ 127                         ; w columns left from here for x -ve

  10+ 9D6A              ;        L *     E   X0mulY0 1>> 1>>  shift >> 16       ;     HL = L * E
  11+ 9D6A              ;        L *   D     Y1mulX0 0   1>>  shift >> 8        ;   DEHL = 00HL  + 0[L*D]0
  12+ 9D6A              ;      H   *     E   X1mulY0 0   1>>  shift >> 8        ;   DEHL = DEHL  + 0[H*E]0 = DEH + 0[H*E]
  13+ 9D6A              ;      H   *   D     X1mulY1 0   0    shift 0           ;  CDE   = CDE   + 0[H*D]
  14+ 9D6A              ; 16 bit HL *  E
  15+ 9D6A              ; start with lower and help with add sequence           ; all with carry flag (as lower case target reg)
  16+ 9D6A              ;        L *     E   X0mulY0 1>> 1>>  shift >> 16       ;     HL = L * E
  17+ 9D6A              ;        L *   D     Y1mulX0 0   1>>  shift >> 8        ;   DEHL = 00HL  + 0[L*D]0
  18+ 9D6A              ;      H   *     E   X1mulY0 0   1>>  shift >> 8        ;   DEHL = DEHL  + 0[H*E]0 = DEH + 0[H*E]
  19+ 9D6A              ;      H   *   D     X1mulY1 0   0    shift 0           ;  CDE   = CDE   + 0[H*D]
  20+ 9D6A
  21+ 9D6A              HLequSRmulQdiv256:  ;X.Y=x1 lo.S*M/256  	\ where M/256 is gradient replaces HLequSRmulQdiv256
  22+ 9D6A 2A B3 85                         ld      hl,(varRS)
  23+ 9D6D 3A B2 85                         ld      a,(varQ)
  24+ 9D70 C5 D5        HLeqyHLmulAdiv256:  push    bc,,de
  25+ 9D72 11 00 00                         ld      de,0        ; de = XY
  26+ 9D75 47                               ld      b,a         ; b = Q
  27+ 9D76                                  ShiftHLRight1
  27+ 9D76 CB 3C       >               srl h
  27+ 9D78 CB 1D       >               rr  l
  28+ 9D7A CB 20                            sla     b
  29+ 9D7C 30 03                            jr      nc,.LL126
  30+ 9D7E EB           .LL125:             ex      de,hl
  31+ 9D7F 19                               add     hl,de
  32+ 9D80 EB                               ex      de,hl       ; de = de + rs
  33+ 9D81              .LL126:             ShiftHLRight1
  33+ 9D81 CB 3C       >               srl h
  33+ 9D83 CB 1D       >               rr  l
  34+ 9D85 CB 20                            sla b
  35+ 9D87 38 F5                            jr      c,.LL125
  36+ 9D89 20 F6                            jr      nz,.LL126
  37+ 9D8B EB                               ex      de,hl   ; hl = result
  38+ 9D8C D1 C1                            pop     bc,,de
  39+ 9D8E C9                               ret
  40+ 9D8F
  41+ 9D8F              ; hl = de * hl where de & hl are small enough to always ne 16 bit result, replaces mulDEbyHL
  42+ 9D8F C5           HLequDEmulHL:       push    bc
  43+ 9D90 7A                               ld      a,d                     ; a = x1
  44+ 9D91 54                               ld      d,h                     ; d = y1
  45+ 9D92 67                               ld      h,a                     ; h = x1
  46+ 9D93 4B                               ld      c,e                     ; c = x0
  47+ 9D94 45                               ld      b,l                     ; b = y0
  48+ 9D95 ED 30                            mul     de                      ; y1 * y0
  49+ 9D97 EB                               ex      de,hl
  50+ 9D98 ED 30                            mul     de                      ; x1 * y0
  51+ 9D9A 19                               add     hl,de                   ; add cross products
  52+ 9D9B 59                               ld      e,c
  53+ 9D9C 50                               ld      d,b
  54+ 9D9D ED 30                            mul     de                      ; y0 * x0
  55+ 9D9F 7D                               ld      a,l                     ; cross products lsb
  56+ 9DA0 82                               add     a,d                     ; add to msb final
  57+ 9DA1 67                               ld      h,a
  58+ 9DA2 6B                               ld      l,e                     ; hl = final
  59+ 9DA3                                  ; 83 cycles, 19 bytes
  60+ 9DA3 AF                               xor     a                       ; reset carry
  61+ 9DA4 C1                               pop     bc
  62+ 9DA5 C9                               ret
  63+ 9DA6              HLequHLmulDEu:
  64+ 9DA6              ;H.L = H.L * D.E unsigned 8.8 (bits 8-23 of the 32 bit product, so truncated), no sign handling
  65+ 9DA6 CD AC 9D                         call    fixedS78_mulu       ; DE.HL = product
  66+ 9DA9 6C                               ld      l,h                 ; l = bits 8-15
  67+ 9DAA 63                               ld      h,e                 ; h = bits 16-23
  68+ 9DAB C9                               ret
  69+ 9DAC              ;DE.HL = D.E * H.L as  7.8 Fixed Point unsigned maths, when doing 24 bit maths scale down to 8.8 as its accurate enough
  70+ 9DAC              fixedS78_mulu:      ;
  71+ 9DAC 7A           .checkZeroMul:      ld      a,d
  72+ 9DAD B3                               or      e
  73+ 9DAE CA D6 9D                         jp      z,.resultIsZero
  74+ 9DB1 7C                               ld      a,h
  75+ 9DB2 B5                               or      l
  76+ 9DB3 CA D6 9D                         jp      z, .resultIsZero
  77+ 9DB6 45           .performMultiplyU:  ld      b,l                 ; b = x0
  78+ 9DB7 4B                               ld      c,e                 ; c =  y0
  79+ 9DB8 5D                               ld      e,l                 ; e = x0
  80+ 9DB9 6A                               ld      l,d                 ; l = y1 d is already y1
  81+ 9DBA E5                               push    hl                  ; save x1 y1 to stack
  82+ 9DBB 69                               ld      l,c                 ; l = y0
  83+ 9DBC ED 30                            mul     de                  ; hl  = y1 * x0
  84+ 9DBE EB                               ex      de,hl               ; . also setting de to x1 y0 as we prepped them in advance
  85+ 9DBF ED 30                            mul     de                  ; x1*y0
  86+ 9DC1                                  ZeroA
  86+ 9DC1 AF          >                        xor a
  87+ 9DC2 19                               add     hl,de               ; sum cross products of y1*x0, x1 * y0 as they require no shifting
  88+ 9DC3 8F                               adc     a,a                 ; and capture carry bit ready for p3
  89+ 9DC4 59                               ld      e,c                 ; de = x0 * y0
  90+ 9DC5 50                               ld      d,b                 ; .
  91+ 9DC6 ED 30                            mul     de                  ; .
  92+ 9DC8 47                               ld      b,a                 ; carry from cross products setting bc to <c>h  (where <c> is carry flag)
  93+ 9DC9 4C                               ld      c,h                 ; .
  94+ 9DCA 7A                               ld      a,d                 ; h = high byte of x0 * y 0 _ lower byte of cross product of y1 * x0
  95+ 9DCB 85                               add     a,l                 ; .
  96+ 9DCC 67                               ld      h,a                 ; .)
  97+ 9DCD 6B                               ld      l,e                 ; so now we have lower btwo bytes of result in HL (p1 p0)
  98+ 9DCE D1                               pop de                      ; get x1 and y1 back from stack into de ready for multiply
  99+ 9DCF ED 30                            mul de                      ; hl = x1*y1 and de = p1 p0
 100+ 9DD1 EB                               ex de,hl                    ; .
 101+ 9DD2 ED 4A                            adc hl,bc                   ; hl = (x1 * y1) + <c>h (where h is upper byte of cross product from above)
 102+ 9DD4 EB                               ex de,hl                    ; swap over de and hl for final result
 103+ 9DD5 C9                               ret
 104+ 9DD6 11 00 00     .resultIsZero:      ld      de,0
 105+ 9DD9 21 00 00                         ld      hl,0
 106+ 9DDC C9                               ret

 535  9E17                  INCLUDE "./Maths/asm_arctan.asm"
# file opened: Maths/asm_arctan.asm
   1+ 9E17              ;Calculate A = arctan(P / Q)
   2+ 9E17              ; This finds the angle in the right-angled triangle where the opposite side to angle A is length P and the adjacent side to angle A has
   3+ 9E17              ; length Q, so:  tan(A) = P / Q
   4+ 9E17              ;
   5+ 9E17              ; The result in A is an integer representing the angle in radians. The routine returns values in the range 0 to 128,  (or 0 to PI radians).
   6+ 9E17 3A 80 84     ARCTAN:                 ld      a,(varP)                    ; LDA P                  \ Set T1 = P EOR Q, which will have the sign of P * Q
   7+ 9E1A 21 B2 85                             ld      hl,varQ                     ; EOR Q
   8+ 9E1D AE                                   xor     (hl)                        ; .
   9+ 9E1E 32 7D 84                             ld      (varT1),a                   ; STA T1
  10+ 9E21 3A B2 85                             ld      a,(varQ)                    ; LDA Q                  \ If Q = 0, jump to AR2 to return a right angle
  11+ 9E24 A7                                   and     a                           ; BEQ AR2
  12+ 9E25 CA 67 9E                             jp      z, .AR2                     ; .
  13+ 9E28 CB 27                                sla     a                           ; ASL A                  \ Set Q = |Q| * 2 (this is a quick way of clearing the
  14+ 9E2A 32 B2 85                             ld      (varQ),a                    ; STA Q                  \ sign bit, and we don't need to shift right again as we only ever use this value in the division with |P| * 2, which we set next)
  15+ 9E2D 3A 80 84                             ld      a,(varP)                    ; LDA P                  \ Set A = |P| * 2
  16+ 9E30 CB 27                                sla     a                           ; ASL A
  17+ 9E32 32 80 84                             ld      (varP),a
  18+ 9E35 21 B2 85                             ld      hl,varQ
  19+ 9E38 BE                                   cp      (hl)                        ; CMP Q                  \ If A >= Q, i.e. |P| > |Q|, jump to AR1 to swap P
  20+ 9E39 D2 4B 9E                             jp      nc, .AR1                    ; BCS AR1                \ and Q around, so we can still use the lookup table
  21+ 9E3C CD 73 9E                             call    ARS1                        ; JSR ARS1               \ Call ARS1 to set the following from the lookup table:  A = arctan(A / Q)  = arctan(|P / Q|)
  22+ 9E3F                                      ClearCarryFlag                      ; SEC                    \ Set the C flag so the SBC instruction in AR3 will be correct, should we jump there
  22+ 9E3F B7          >                        or a
  23+ 9E40 4F           .AR4:                   ld      c,a                         ; as we have to use a we use c as a temp, we can't push af as we would loose flags on pop
  24+ 9E41 3A 7D 84                             ld      a,(varT1)                   ; LDX T1                 \ If T1 is negative, i.e. P and Q have different signs,
  25+ 9E44 47                                   ld      b,a                         ; .
  26+ 9E45 A7                                   and     a                           ; BMI AR3                \ jump down to AR3 to return arctan(-|P / Q|)
  27+ 9E46 79                                   ld      a,c                         ; .                      \ we need to get a back before jump
  28+ 9E47 FA 6A 9E                             jp      m, .AR3                     ; .
  29+ 9E4A C9                                   ret                                 ; RTS                    \ Otherwise P and Q have the same sign, so our result is correct and we can return from the subroutine
  30+ 9E4B              ; We want to calculate arctan(t) where |t| > 1, so we can use the calculation described in the documentation for the ACT table, i.e. 64 - arctan(1 / t)
  31+ 9E4B              ; In the 6502 verion it works with A already being P but we will fetch it
  32+ 9E4B 3A B2 85     .AR1:                   ld      a,(varQ)                    ; LDX Q                  \ Swap the values in Q and P, using the fact that we
  33+ 9E4E 47                                   ld      b,a                         ; .
  34+ 9E4F 3A 80 84                             ld      a,(varP)                    ; STA Q                  \ called AR1 with A = P
  35+ 9E52 32 B2 85                             ld      (varQ),a                    ; .
  36+ 9E55 78                                   ld      a,b                         ; TXA                    \ This also sets A = P (which now contains the original argument |Q|)
  37+ 9E56 32 80 84                             ld      (varP),a                    ; STX P                  \
  38+ 9E59 CD 73 9E                             call    ARS1                        ; JSR ARS1               \ Call ARS1 to set the following from the lookup table: A = arctan(A / Q) = arctan(|Q / P|) = arctan(1 / |P / Q|)
  39+ 9E5C 32 CE 85                             ld      (varT),a                    ; STA T                  \ Set T = 64 - T, we use B as T (its not really that)
  40+ 9E5F 47                                   ld      b,a                         ; its actually t = a, a = 64-a
  41+ 9E60 3E 40                                ld      a,64                        ; LDA #64 What is going on here is t = result
  42+ 9E62                                      ClearCarryFlag                      ; SBC T                            a = 64- result
  42+ 9E62 B7          >                        or a
  43+ 9E63 98                                   sbc     a,b                         ; .
  44+ 9E64 C3 40 9E                             jp      .AR4                        ; BCS AR4                \ Jump to AR4 to continue the calculation (this BCS is effectively a JMP as the subtraction will never underflow, as ARS1 returns values in the range 0-31)
  45+ 9E67              ; If we get here then Q = 0, so tan(A) = infinity and A is a right angle, or 0.25 of a circle. We allocate 255 to a full circle, so we should return 63 for a right angle
  46+ 9E67 3E 3F        .AR2:                   ld      a,63                        ; LDA #63                \ Set A to 63, to represent a right angle
  47+ 9E69 C9                                   ret                                 ; RTS                    \ Return from the subroutine
  48+ 9E6A              ; A contains arctan(|P / Q|) but P and Q have different signs, so we need to return arctan(-|P / Q|), using the calculation described in the documentation for the ACT table, i.e. 128 - A
  49+ 9E6A 32 CE 85     .AR3:                   ld      (varT),a
  50+ 9E6D 47                                   ld      b,a                         ; STA T                  \ Set A = 128 - A, we use b as T
  51+ 9E6E 3E 80                                ld      a,128                       ; LDA #128               \
  52+ 9E70                                      ClearCarryFlag                      ; SBC T                  \ The subtraction will work because we did a SEC before calling AR3
  52+ 9E70 B7          >                        or a
  53+ 9E71 98                                   sbc     a,b
  54+ 9E72 C9                                   ret                                 ; RTS                    \ Return from the subroutine
  55+ 9E73              ; This routine fetches arctan(A / Q) from the ACT table, so A will be set to an integer in the range 0 to 31 that represents an angle from 0 to 45 degrees (or 0 to \ PI / 4 radians)
  56+ 9E73              ARS1:                   MMUSelectMathsTables
  56+ 9E73 ED 91 50 63 >                     nextreg MathsTablesMMU,    BankMathsTables
  57+ 9E77 CD A7 07                             call    Amul256DivQ                 ; JSR LL28               \ Call LL28 to calculate: R = 256 * A / Q
  58+ 9E7A 3A B3 85                             ld      a,(varR)                    ; LDA R                  \ Set X = R / 8
  59+ 9E7D CB 3F                                srl     a                           ; LSR A                  \       = 32 * A / Q
  60+ 9E7F CB 3F                                srl     a                           ; LSR A                  \
  61+ 9E81 CB 3F                                srl     a                           ; LSR A                  \ so X has the value t * 32 where t = A / Q, which is
  62+ 9E83 21 AA 9E                             ld      hl,ACT                      ; TAX                    \ what we need to look up values in the ACT table
  63+ 9E86 ED 31                                add     hl,a                        ; LDA ACT,X              \ Fetch ACT+X from the ACT table into A, so now:
  64+ 9E88 7E                                   ld      a,(hl)                      ;                        \   A = value in ACT + X = value in ACT + (32 * A / Q)= arctan(A / Q)
  65+ 9E89 C9                                   ret                                 ; RTS                    \ Return from the subroutine
  66+ 9E8A

   1+ 9FB2              ; A = A / D * 96 unsigned (A < D, else 96), the 6502 TIS2 shift and subtract. The remainder is 9 bit after each shift:
   2+ 9FB2              ; when the shift carries out it is over 255 so over D and must be subtracted (that carry was once dropped, so with D
   3+ 9FB2              ; over 128 the answer could be anything, e.g. 67 / 137 gave 1 not 46)
   4+ 9FB2              AequAdivQmul96ABS:      JumpIfAGTENusng d, .TIS2AccGTEQ			; if A >= Q then return with a 1 (unity i.e. 96) with the correct sign
   4+ 9FB2 BA          >                        cp     d
   4+ 9FB3 D2 D0 9F    >                        jp		nc,.TIS2AccGTEQ
   5+ 9FB6 06 FE                                ld			b,$FE						; division roll (replaced varT)
   6+ 9FB8 CB 27        .TIS2RollTLoop:			sla			a
   7+ 9FBA 38 04                                jr          c,.TIS2Sub                  ; 9 bit remainder >= 256 > d
   8+ 9FBC                                      JumpIfALTNusng d,.TIS2SkipSub           ; a < d so don;t subtract
   8+ 9FBC BA          >                        cp      d
   8+ 9FBD DA D3 9F    >                        jp		c, .TIS2SkipSub
   9+ 9FC0 92           .TIS2Sub:               sub			d							; remainder - d (mod 256 is right for the 9 bit case)
  10+ 9FC1 37                                   scf
  11+ 9FC2 CB 10                                rl			b							; T rolled left to push bit out the end
  12+ 9FC4 38 F2                                jr			c,.TIS2RollTLoop				; if we still have not hit the empty marker continue
  13+ 9FC6 78           .TIS2SKIPCont:	        ld			a,b							; T
  14+ 9FC7 CB 3F                                srl			a							; result / 2
  15+ 9FC9 CB 3F                                srl			a							; result / 4
  16+ 9FCB 47                                   ld			b,a							; t = t /4
  17+ 9FCC CB 3F                                srl			a							; result / 8
  18+ 9FCE 80                                   add			a,b							; result /8 + result /4
  19+ 9FCF C9                                   ret

  25+ 9FD8 C3 C6 9F                             jp			.TIS2SKIPCont

 546  A09B                  INCLUDE "./Maths/Utilities/badd_ll38.asm"
# file opened: Maths/Utilities/badd_ll38.asm
   1+ A09B              baddll38:				;.LL38	\ -> &4812 \ BADD(S)A=R+Q(SA) \ byte add (subtract)   (Sign S)A = R + Q*(Sign from A^S)
   2+ A09B              SAEquSRPlusAQ:
   3+ A09B              ; Calculate the following between sign-magnitude numbers:
   4+ A09B              ;   (S A) = (S R) + (A Q)
   5+ A09B              ; where the sign bytes only contain the sign bits, not magnitudes.
   6+ A09B              ; note goes wrong at <-127 >128 so need 16 bit version
   7+ A09B              ; so need to fix the issue with carry flag not returning a fault correctly
   8+ A09B              LL38:
   9+ A09B              ; calculation table
  10+ A09B              ;   R     Q    Op            Sign calc
  11+ A09B              ;	10    5    Add           +    sign same add R sign
  12+ A09B              ;   -10   5    ABS Sub       -    sign diff ABS R > S sub R sign
  13+ A09B              ;   10   -5    ABS sub       +    sign diff ABS R > S sub R sign
  14+ A09B              ;	-10  -5    ABS Add       -    sign same add R sign
  15+ A09B              ;   5    10    Add           +    sign same add R sign
  16+ A09B              ;   -5   10    Swap ABS SUB  +    sign diff ABS Q > R swap SUB Q sign
  17+ A09B              ;   5    -10   swap ABS Sub  -    sign diff ABS Q > R swap SUB R sign
  18+ A09B              ;   -5   -10   ABS  add      -    sign same add R sign

  20+ A09B              ;   -10   5    ABS Sub       -    sign diff ABS R > S sub R sign
  21+ A09B              ;   10   -5    ABS sub       +    sign diff ABS R > S sub R sign
  22+ A09B              ;   -5   10    Swap ABS SUB  +    sign diff ABS Q > R swap SUB Q sign
  23+ A09B              ;   5    -10   swap ABS Sub  -    sign diff ABS Q > R swap SUB R sign

  26+ A09B              ; Calculate sign for Q from A and varS
  27+ A09B 21 B4 85     	ld		hl,varS							;
  28+ A09E AE           	xor		(hl)							;  EOR &83		\ S	\ sign of operator is A xor S
  29+ A09F FA AA A0     	jp		m,.LL39Subtraction  			; if signs are different then we have subtraction
  30+ A0A2 3A B2 85     	ld		a,(varQ)						; Q	\ else addition, S already correct
  31+ A0A5 21 B3 85     	ld		hl,varR
  32+ A0A8 86           	add		a,(hl)							; a = Q + R
  33+ A0A9 C9           	ret										; Done carry set if overflow
  34+ A0AA              .LL39Subtraction:							; 1 byte subtraction (S)A = R-Q
  35+ A0AA 3A B3 85     	ld		a,(varR)						; a = R
  36+ A0AD 21 B2 85     	ld		hl,varQ                         ; Q
  37+ A0B0              ;--	JumpIfALTMemHLusng LL39SwapSubtraction	; if a < (hl) then do LL39SwapSubtraction
  38+ A0B0              	ClearCarryFlag                          ; we need to not use carry (6502 is different that it uses the compliement)
  38+ A0B0 B7          >                        or a
  39+ A0B1 9E           	sbc		a,(hl)							; A = R - Q which as R >= Q will always be a positive result
  40+ A0B2 38 01            jr      c,.LL39SignCorrection
  41+ A0B4              ;--    jr      a,.LL39ResultZero
  42+ A0B4              ;--   JumpIfNegative LL39SignCorrection		; if there was underflow we have to correct sign
  43+ A0B4              ;--	or		a								; Clear carry flag to say result is correct
  44+ A0B4 C9           	ret
  45+ A0B5              .LL39SignCorrection:
  46+ A0B5 FE 00            cp      0                               ; if its 0 then neg will affect flag so we just zero result to save compute
  47+ A0B7 28 0E            jr      z,.LL39ResultZero
  48+ A0B9 ED 44            neg                                     ; flip A 2'c value to positive
  49+ A0BB 08           	ex		af,af'							; save A temporarily
  50+ A0BC 3A B4 85     	ld		a,(varS)						; Flip Sign bit in varS
  51+ A0BF EE 80        	xor		$80							    ;
  52+ A0C1 32 B4 85     	ld		(varS),a                        ; flip sign bit of a
  53+ A0C4 08           	ex		af,af'                          ; get back a which is the result
  54+ A0C5                  ClearCarryFlag                          ; clear carry as NEG instrunction sets it for non zero
  54+ A0C5 B7          >                        or a
  55+ A0C6 C9           	ret
  56+ A0C7              .LL39ResultZero:
  57+ A0C7 32 B4 85         ld      (varS),a                        ; a is zero at this stage so set sign as well
  58+ A0CA                  ClearCarryFlag                          ; clear carry
  58+ A0CA B7          >                        or a
  59+ A0CB C9               ret
  60+ A0CC              ;--LL39SwapSubtraction:
  61+ A0CC              ;--	push	bc
  62+ A0CC              ;--	ld		b,a
  63+ A0CC              ;--	ld		a,(hl)
  64+ A0CC              ;--	sub		b
  65+ A0CC              ;--	pop		bc
  66+ A0CC              ;--	ex		af,af'							; do we flip here or negate. i think its flip as its overflowed unsigned
  67+ A0CC              ;--	ld		a,(varS)
  68+ A0CC              ;--	xor		$80
  69+ A0CC              ;--	ld		(varS),a
  70+ A0CC              ;--	ex		af,af'
  71+ A0CC              ;--	ret

 181++A534              ; AHL = BHL + CDE in S15.8 lead sign, saturating. AHLequBHLplusCDE does not detect overflow: with the same signs a magnitude
 182++A534              ; sum >= 32768.0 carries into bit 7 and flips the sign, which would point the missile the wrong way. Opposite signs can not

   1+ C6C3              ;----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
   2+ C6C3              ; The system map (the extended keyboard's EDIT key, in flight): a flat top down map of the local system round us, x across
   3+ C6C3              ; and z up the screen (ahead is up, as we always look along z), y (height) left out of the plot and shown as a + / - number
   4+ C6C3              ; of units beside each body. The sun, the planet and the space station are marked and named, other ships are dots (red if
   5+ C6C3              ; hostile). The scale is a power of 2 chosen so the sun, planet and station all fit; ships further out are left off.
   6+ C6C3              ; Positions come from SystemMapGather (main memory, as the sun, planet and ship banks page into slot 6, where this code
   7+ C6C3              ; is). It is redrawn twice a second (loop_system_map), erasing only what it drew the time before, so it doesn't flicker.
   8+ C6C3              ; In BankMenuSystem with the system data screen.
   9+ C6C3              ;----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  10+ C6C3              SMapCentreX             equ 160                     ; us
  11+ C6C3              SMapCentreY             equ 134
  12+ C6C3              SMapRadius              equ 104                     ; the furthest a mark is drawn from us on either axis
  13+ C6C3              SMapRefreshFrames       equ FramesPerSecond / 2

  15+ C6C3              SMapPrevSize            equ 8                       ; per mark drawn: in use, row, column (2), label row, label column (2), label length
  16+ C6C3              SMapAxisColour          equ L2ColourGREY_4
  17+ C6C3              SMapTextRow             equ 244

   1+ E2F7              ; The layer 2 page shown and the shadow (draw) page are kept here rather than read back with GetNextReg, so the flip
   2+ E2F7              ; needs no interrupt protection: it's called from main code, from the attract mode interrupt and at startup with
   3+ E2F7              ; interrupts off (l2_initialise). l2_initialise and l2_320_initialise are the only other writers of the two registers.
   4+ E2F7 08           l2_page_shown           DB      LAYER2_SCREEN_BANK1         ; (these two must stay together, read as a pair)
   5+ E2F8 0D           l2_page_shadow          DB      LAYER2_SHADOW_BANK1
   6+ E2F9
   7+ E2F9 ED 5B F7 E2  l2_flip_buffers:        ld      de,(l2_page_shown)          ; e = shown, d = shadow
   8+ E2FD 7A                                   ld      a,d                         ; the shadow page goes on screen
   9+ E2FE ED 92 12                             nextreg LAYER2_RAM_PAGE_REGISTER, a
  10+ E301 7B                                   ld      a,e                         ; and what was shown becomes the shadow
  11+ E302 ED 92 13                             nextreg LAYER2_RAM_SHADOW_REGISTER, a
  12+ E305 7A                                   ld      a,d                         ; swap the pair
  13+ E306 53                                   ld      d,e                         ; .
  14+ E307 5F                                   ld      e,a                         ; .
  15+ E308 ED 53 F7 E2                          ld      (l2_page_shown),de          ; .
  16+ E30C C9                                   ret

  62+ EC34              ; l2_draw_6502_line - clip and draw a line in the Layer 2 upper two thirds (256x128, rows 0-63 bank 0, rows 64-127 bank 1)
  63+ EC34              ; In : x1,y1,x2,y2 16 bit signed, nominally -1024..+1024 (any value within +/-2047 is safe)
  64+ EC34              ;      colour from line_gfx_colour, Layer 2 code bank paged in (MMUSelectLayer2)
  65+ EC34              ; Out: carry set   - line wholly outside the window, nothing drawn
  66+ EC34              ;      carry clear - line drawn, x1,y1,x2,y2 hold the clipped end points (high bytes 0)
  67+ EC34              ;      AF, BC, DE, HL, AF' destroyed, IX and IY preserved
  68+ EC34              ; y1 = y2           horizontal, clamped without any maths, P1 = P2 plots a single pixel, long spans are a DMA fill
  69+ EC34              ; x1 = x2           vertical, clamped without any maths, column fill split at the bank 0/1 boundary
  70+ EC34              ; otherwise         Cohen-Sutherland outcodes for trivial accept/reject, edge intersections via 12x12 multiply and
  71+ EC34              ;                   24/16 divide (rounded), then the clipped line is re-checked for pixel/horz/vert before an 8 bit Bresenham
  72+ EC34              ;----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  73+ EC34              L2L_OC_LEFT_BIT         equ     0
  74+ EC34              L2L_OC_RIGHT_BIT        equ     1

   1+ F042              ;----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
   2+ F042              ; l2_fill_convex_polygon: a convex polygon filled in the 256 x 128 view (256 x 192 Layer 2, rows 0 to 127), for solid ships
   3+ F042              ; (SOLID_HULL, Documentation/SolidHulls.md). Assembled in every build so it can be tested on its own.
   4+ F042              ;   in:  ix = points, b of them (3 to PolyMaxPoints): x lo, x hi, y lo, y hi each, 16 bit 2's complement (off screen is
   5+ F042              ;        fine), a = colour
   6+ F042              ;   out: nothing; uses every register
   7+ F042              ; Each edge is walked row by row from its top to its bottom (rows clipped to the view first), with x exact:
   8+ F042              ; x(y) = xa + sign(dx) * floor((y - ya) * |dx| / dy), stepped as q = |dx| / dy, r = |dx| mod dy per row (one divide an
   9+ F042              ; edge, and a 32 / 16 divide to start an edge that begins above the view). Each row keeps its smallest and largest x
  10+ F042              ; (16 bit, so a polygon partly off the side is right), then each row's span is clipped to columns 0 to 255 and drawn with
  11+ F042              ; l2_draw_horz_line. Both ends of every span are drawn, so faces that share an edge meet with no gap. No winding needed.
  12+ F042              ; A flat polygon (every point on one row) is that row from its smallest to its largest x.
  13+ F042              ; Tools/test_lines.py test_fill_convex_polygon checks it pixel for pixel against the same rules in Python
  14+ F042              PolyMaxPoints           equ 8
  15+ F042              PolyViewRows            equ 128
  16+ F042

  18+ F043 00           PolyCount               DB 0

  21+ F047 00           PolyBottom              DB 0

   1+ F597              ;----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
   2+ F597              ; Solid ships (SOLID_HULL, Documentation/SolidHulls.md): SolidHullDraw, from ProcessShip after CullV2 with the ship's
   3+ F597              ; universe bank in slot 6 and this (the Layer 2) bank in slot 7.
   4+ F597              ;   carry set: drawn solid. In order: the hull's faces (sorted), the phase 2 polygons (ports: engines, later entrances
   5+ F597              ;   and view ports), with SOLID_OUTLINES lines over it (ALL every visible edge, DECORATION only the decoration edges),
   6+ F597              ;   then the table's lone lines (nose sensor / gun port lines, unless ALL drew them); carry clear: the caller draws the
   7+ F597              ;   wireframe
   8+ F597              ; Drawn solid when the model has a face table (Tools/ship_faces.py: ShipSolidFlag $00, copied to UBnkHullSolid), no vertex
   9+ F597              ; is at or behind the camera (its z from ProcessNodes, in UBnkNodeArray2), and with WIREFRAME_FALLBACK its z is not less
  10+ F597              ; than WIREFRAME_DISTANCE (eliteNext.asm). The table's polygons are the faces plus any fins (a fin is seen when any face
  11+ F597              ; its edges are on faces us). The visible ones are painted furthest first (painter's algorithm), each one's depth its
  12+ F597              ; furthest vertex, so on a hull that isn't convex a nearer face covers a further one. Colours, for now: a batch of 4 per
  13+ F597              ; ship (by model id), alternating through the faces so each can be seen
  14+ F597                  IFDEF SOLID_HULL
  15+ F597              SolidMaxFaces           equ 16
  16+ F597 00 00 00...  SolidFaceList           DS SolidMaxFaces * 5        ; per visible face: depth (16 bit), face table record (16 bit), face nbr
  17+ F5E7 00           SolidFaceCount          DB 0
  18+ F5E8 00 00 00...  SolidPoints             DS PolyMaxPoints * 4        ; a face's screen points for l2_fill_convex_polygon
  19+ F608 00           SolidFaceNbr            DB 0                        ; the record being looked at
  20+ F609 00 00        SolidVisMask            DW 0                        ; bit f: face f faces us
  21+ F60B 00 00        SolidLinesAt            DW 0                        ; the face table's lone lines
  22+ F60D 00 00        SolidLateAt             DW 0                        ; its phase 2 polygons (ports)
  23+ F60F 49           SolidPortColours        DB $49                      ; PortEngine: dark grey (later a thrust colour while manoeuvring)
  24+ F610 00                                   DB $00                      ; PortEntrance: black
  25+ F611 00           SolidColour             DB 0
  26+ F612              ; RGB 332, 4 a ship, never $E3 (the transparent colour)
  27+ F612 E0 A0 E4 80  SolidColours            DB $E0, $A0, $E4, $80       ; reds

  29+ F61A 03 02 27 01                          DB $03, $02, $27, $01       ; blues

  39+ F637                                  IFDEF WIREFRAME_FALLBACK

 731  F85D                  INCLUDE "./Layer2Graphics/l2_draw_line_v2.asm"
# file opened: Layer2Graphics/l2_draw_line_v2.asm
   1+ F85D              ; ******************************************************************************
   2+ F85D              ;
   3+ F85D              ;	Draw a pixel line from (x0,y0) defined in (COORDS) - the current plot
   4+ F85D              ;	coordinate, to the relative distance points (x0+x,y0+y).
   5+ F85D              ;
   6+ F85D              ;	Design & programming by Gunther Strube,	Copyright (C) InterLogic 1995
   7+ F85D              ;
   8+ F85D              ;	The (COORDS+0)	pointer contains the current y coordinate, (COORDS+1) the
   9+ F85D              ;	current x coordinate. The main program should reset the (COORDS) variables
  10+ F85D              ;	before using line drawing.
  11+ F85D              ;
  12+ F85D              ;	The routine checks the range of specified coordinates which is the
  13+ F85D              ;	boundaries of the graphics area (256x64	pixels).
  14+ F85D              ;	If a boundary error occurs the routine exits automatically.	This may be
  15+ F85D              ;	useful if you are trying to draw a line longer than allowed. Only the
  16+ F85D              ;	visible part will be drawn.
  17+ F85D              ;
  18+ F85D              ;	The hardware graphics memory is organized as (0,0) in the top left corner.
  19+ F85D              ;
  20+ F85D              ;	The plot routine is	defined by an address pointer	in IX.
  21+ F85D              ;
  22+ F85D              ;	IN:	HL =	move	relative x horisontal points (maximum +/- 255).
  23+ F85D              ;		DE =	move	relative y vertical	points (maximum +/-	255).
  24+ F85D              ;		IX =	pointer to plot routine that uses HL = (x,y)	of plot coordinate.
  25+ F85D              ;
  26+ F85D              ;	OUT:	None.
  27+ F85D              ;
  28+ F85D              ;	Registers	used	by routine:
  29+ F85D              ;		   N	:	B, loop counter
  30+ F85D              ;		   i	:	line	balance variable
  31+ F85D              ;		   x	:	H/L,	horisontal, vertical distance	variables
  32+ F85D              ;		   y	:	H/L,	horisontal, vertical distance	variables
  33+ F85D              ;	  (x0,y0)	:	(h,l)
  34+ F85D              ;	  direc_x	:	d, horisontal step increment
  35+ F85D              ;	  direc_y	:	e, vertical step increment
  36+ F85D              ;		 ddx	:	b, horisontal step increment
  37+ F85D              ;		 ddy	:	c, vertical step increment
  38+ F85D              ;
  39+ F85D              ;		DE, A work registers.
  40+ F85D              ;
  41+ F85D              ; The algorithm in pseudo-code:
  42+ F85D              ;
  43+ F85D              ;	direc_x =	SGN x: direc_y	= SGN y
  44+ F85D              ;	x = ABS x: y =	ABS y
  45+ F85D              ;
  46+ F85D              ;	if x	>= y
  47+ F85D              ;		if x+y=0 then return
  48+ F85D              ;		H = x
  49+ F85D              ;		L = y
  50+ F85D              ;		ddx = direc_x
  51+ F85D              ;		ddy = 0
  52+ F85D              ;	else
  53+ F85D              ;		H = y
  54+ F85D              ;		L = x
  55+ F85D              ;		ddx = 0
  56+ F85D              ;		ddy = direc_y
  57+ F85D              ;	endif
  58+ F85D              ;
  59+ F85D              ;	B = H
  60+ F85D              ;	i = INT(B/2)
  61+ F85D              ;	FOR N=B TO 1 STEP -1
  62+ F85D              ;		i = i + L
  63+ F85D              ;		if i	< H
  64+ F85D              ;			ix =	ddx
  65+ F85D              ;			iy =	ddy
  66+ F85D              ;		else
  67+ F85D              ;			i = i - H
  68+ F85D              ;			ix =	direc_x
  69+ F85D              ;			iy =	direc_y
  70+ F85D              ;		endif
  71+ F85D              ;		x0 =	x0 +	ix
  72+ F85D              ;		y0 =	y0 +	iy
  73+ F85D              ;		plot	(x0,y0)
  74+ F85D              ;	NEXT	N
  75+ F85D              ;
  76+ F85D              ;
  77+ F85D              ;	Registers	changed after return:
  78+ F85D              ;		..BCDEHL/IXIY/af......	same
  79+ F85D              ;		AF....../..../..bcdehl	different
  80+ F85D              ;
  81+ F85D 00 00        line_gfx_coords         dw  0
  82+ F85F
  83+ F85F              LineHLtoDE:
  84+ F85F 7C           TestMaxY:               ld	a,h ; were h = y or l = y?
  85+ F860 FE C0                                cp	192
  86+ F862 30 26                                jr	nc, exit_line		; y0	coordinate out	of range
  87+ F864 7A                                   ld	a,d
  88+ F865 FE C0                                cp	192
  89+ F867 30 21                                jr	nc, exit_line		; y1	coordinate out	of range
  90+ F869 22 5D F8                             ld	(line_gfx_coords),hl		; the starting	point is now default
  91+ F86C E5                                   push	hl
  92+ F86D D5                                   push	de
  93+ F86E 6C                                   ld	l,h				; L = x0
  94+ F86F 62                                   ld	h,d				; H = x1
  95+ F870 7C           distanceX:		        ld	a,h
  96+ F871 95                                   sub	l
  97+ F872 6F                                   ld	l,a
  98+ F873 26 00                                ld	h,0
  99+ F875 30 02                                jr	nc, distanceXDone
 100+ F877 26 FF                                ld	h,-1
 101+ F879 D1           distanceXDone:          pop	de
 102+ F87A E3                                   ex	(sp),hl			; L = y0
 103+ F87B 63                                   ld	h,e				; H = y1
 104+ F87C 7C           distanceY:		        ld	a,h
 105+ F87D 95                                   sub	l
 106+ F87E 6F                                   ld	l,a
 107+ F87F 26 00                                ld	h,0
 108+ F881 30 02                                jr	nc, distanceYDone
 109+ F883 26 FF                                ld	h,-1
 110+ F885 D1           distanceYDone:          pop	de
 111+ F886 EB                                   ex	de,hl			; h.dist.	= HL, v.dist. = DE
 112+ F887 CD 8B F8                             call	DrawLineRelative			; draw line...
 113+ F88A C9           exit_line:              ret

 208+ F906              ; ******************************************************************************

 210+ F906              ;	SGN (Signum value) of 16	bit signed integer.

 209+ E0BC              ; Creates a 32x32 sprite based on first sprite number and pattern, then goes:
 210+ E0BC              ;    Spr,   pattern     spr+1, pattern+1
 211+ E0BC              ;    Spr+1, pattern+2   spr+3, pattern+3
 212+ E0BC              ; " sprite_big BC = row, hl= col D = sprite nbr , E= , pattern"
 213+ E0BC              ; note, BC and HL must be in correct range else they will mess up other byte's attributes, not masked for speed
 214+ E0BC              ; note this is based on full screen sprites including writing to border
 215+ E0BC              ; Currently can not get realtive sprites to work so will brute force it.

 144++C0BE              ; Flags work as follows:
 145++C0BE              ; UBnKSpawnObject - signals on death to spawn cargo items
 146++C0BE              ; 0 -                   Spawn Cargo 1
 147++C0BE              ; 1 -                   Spawn Cargo 2
 148++C0BE              ; 2 -                   Spawn Cargo 3
 149++C0BE              ; 3 -                   Spawn Cargo 4
